title: Causal-DFM: Diffusion-Based Causal-Invariant Dynamic Factor Model for Stock Return Prediction

problem.claim: Stock return prediction is highly sensitive to market regime shifts because statistical relationships between observed features and returns can change abruptly.

gap.claim: Deep learning-based factor models often rely on correlations specific to historical market environments, causing learned patterns to break down under different regimes and producing severe out-of-distribution degradation.

contributions.claim: Causal-DFM is a causality-inspired factor-based framework that encourages compact, stable return-relevant representations while suppressing environment-dependent variations.
The framework couples a conditional diffusion factor prior for regime-varying market dynamics with an Information-Bottleneck-regularized Transformer state encoder.
The paper presents an information-theoretic analysis motivating the objective and describing conditions for alignment with stable return mechanisms across environments.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on real-world stock datasets reportedly show that Causal-DFM consistently outperforms strong baselines.
The reported gains are particularly pronounced during regime transitions and crisis periods.
The source code is reported to be available at https://github.com/bjtu-yzh/Causal-DFM.

narrative_sequence.summary: Market regime shifts can abruptly change feature-return relationships and challenge stock return prediction.
Existing deep learning factor models may depend on regime-specific correlations and degrade out of distribution.
Causal-DFM combines stable representation learning with suppression of environment-dependent variation.
An information-theoretic analysis motivates the objective and its cross-environment alignment conditions.
Experiments reportedly show stronger performance, especially during regime transitions and crises.

source_observation.claim: The framework combines a regime-varying factor prior with a capacity-controlled, return-predictive representation.

interpretation.claim: Modeling changing systematic dynamics while limiting representation capacity may reduce reliance on spurious regime-specific signals.

application.claim: For prediction under distribution shift, pair explicit environment-dynamics modeling with a compact representation objective.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether the approach generalizes beyond the reported stock datasets or market-regime setting.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the datasets, baselines, evaluation metrics, or quantitative performance differences.
The abstract does not provide implementation details sufficient to assess reproducibility.
The abstract does not report ablations separating the diffusion prior, Transformer encoder, and Information Bottleneck components.
